newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up, light US buying seen.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up, light US buying seen.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on technical adjustment, and light U.S. buying was seen in a market otherwise void of demand, dealers said.
"It's still very thin...save for some hand-to-mouth covering," a dealer said, describing the day's trade.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted June RSS1 buyer at 275.50 cents ($1.08) a kg, up 2.50 cents from Wednesday. June SMR 20 buyer ended two cents up to 260.50 cents.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 260 cents, SMR CV at 271, SMR L at 307 cents, SMR 5 at 271, SMR 10 at 261 and drum latex at 229 cents.
The INRO five-day average rose to 208.17 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on May 14, compared to 207.49 on May 13.
The daily indicator climbed to 210.51 from 208.34 previously.
